elements.description: The "working…" panel of an AI chat: steps and searches appear one by one, then "Worked for …".

properties.name: stepMs
properties.description: Pause between two steps, in ms (the timeline that runs when `progress` and `done` are unset)

properties.name: progress
properties.description: How many steps have appeared; unset, the timeline reveals them

properties.name: done
properties.description: Finished; unset, the timeline decides (when `progress` is unset too)

properties.name: loop
properties.description:
Start over after a pause once finished – only while the timeline runs everything. Stops after a few runs, and
as soon as the pointer or focus is inside (WCAG 2.2.2)

properties.name: startedAt
properties.description: When the work started, in epoch ms – the header's timer counts from here. Defaults to when the run started

properties.name: look
properties.description: Visual style: "standard" or "clean"; unset follows <tc-look-provider>, else "standard"

events.name: tc-progress-change
events.description: The timeline revealed a step; detail `{ progress: number }`, how many steps show

events.name: tc-done
events.description: It finished (by the timeline or by `done`); detail `{ seconds: number }`, how long it worked

events.name: tc-open-change
events.description: The header was clicked, or a new run unfolded the steps; detail `{ open: boolean }`. Cancelable: preventDefault() keeps `open` as it is (controlled use)

props.name: onProgressChange
props.description: Reports each step the timeline reveals

props.name: onDone
props.description: Called once it's finished – by the timeline or by `done` – with the seconds it worked

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the steps are unfolded (controlled when defined)

changelog: thinking-state no longer reports `onOpenChange(true)` on mount when `open` is held false; date-range-picker doesn't flash its "Last 30 days" stand-in before reading today; memory-panel with `undoFor={Infinity}` keeps a failure message instead of clearing it at once; dropzone keeps focus on a row while another row folds away (the React version lost it in real browsers).
